questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: In the beginning, my plans were to go on exchange with my sister and our friend, but we all study different things, so we had to find a suitable city for all of us. We wanted a place that were not to big and seemed like it had a lot to offer culturally, a lot to explore in terms of food, museums, thrift shops and so on. Basically we picked mostly based off on vibes.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: depends on what information you mean by this question. Charles University were great at giving information about arrival dates, how to pick your classes and so on. They organized a online Q&A a couple of weeks before the start of university and the erasmus coordinators/staff were easy to get a hold on, through e-mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Charles university had a "buddy system" were you (through a fancy website) got assigned to a person studying at Charles and the idea was that they could help you with questions and so on. I reached out to my buddy but they never answered me and never (as far as im aware) tried to come in contact with me. I didn't meet anyone during my stay, that used the buddy system.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: i would really recommend joining different erasmus groups on whatsapp and facebook, a lot of people are looking for roomates on there, that is how i found housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: off campus in Prague is not really a big deal, the universities are scattered around the city, so you cant really live to far away. I heard mixed opinions about the dorms that they offer. I do think its a great opportunity, because its very cheap, IF you dont mind living with a roomate. They are only 30/40 minutes away from the inner city, easy to get around with public transportation is easy. Some of the dorms had problems with bed bugs and stuff like that, so be aware. The one in Hostivar seemed like the best one (no bed bugs)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: uuuh i dont remember much. I think we just went to the university and they gave us some documents. Pretty easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: they had an office for erasmus students, which where open a couple times a week, with some very nice staff. You could also call and write them over e-mail. At the faculty of arts they also have a minitaure horse (Monty) who says hello every second wednesday.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: they registration for classes were a bit stressfull. The website is old and can be annoying. I ended up only getting one of the classes off of my pre-approaval, the rest were just classes i found during the registration period. Some classes gets filled up pretty quickly, i think they let the czech students choose first. It took some time to make everything work within the same schedule, a lot of the classes are at the same time or starts right after eachother, which makes it difficult. But there are a lot of different classes too choose from.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: With classes, try and go to as many as possible during the registration period, to see which classes seems most like something you would like, a lot of the times the classes are different to the describtion online. Its really hard to get all of the classes you want, but i ended up enjoying everything, so dont worry too much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of my classes were literature classes, which meant a lot of the students were from England/Ireland and obviously everything we read was in english, a lot of my classes were based on english literature in some sense. So you need to have a good understanding of english and be able to read well in english as well. It really depends on the professor, how high the academic level is or what they expect from you. Some classes i took wanted us to do a lot of presentations, and i would say that i had quit a lot of homework, very heavy on reading. But i never felt like it was too much, the classes are pretty chill and the professors are nice.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
You dont participate as much, its a lot of listening and i felt the classes lacked a more open discussion. The classes go on for two hours with no
breaks...how
engaged the proffessors was with the students and their interest in our opinions varied a lot. Some of my classes were great and inspiring, some were just okay. But overall i would say i enjoyed it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Contemporary Fiction Post-2020 - Small Presses	
Writing as Experiment: Writers on Writing		
Hermits, Wives, Queens, and Schemers: Women in Medieval & Early Modern Literature
Slovene women writers at the beginning of the 20th Century		 	
World Literature and the World of Literature: the Albanian Reality	
Interpretation of European Fairytales

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i would recommend Hermits, Wives, Queens and schemers, the proffesors were great and actually interested in us students. I also enjoyed World literature and the world of literature: the albanian reality and slovene women writers at the beginning of the 20th century

questions.answer: nothing unexpected really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: housing were a bit more expensive that i expected, food and drinks and stuff were quite cheap. Everything is cheap in Prague and definently a lot cheaper than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: the erasmus student network under charles university hosted different day and weekendtrips out of the city, pubquizzez, sightseeing and stuff like that. Mostly in beginning, as far as im aware.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: sign up for some stuff through ESN if you want to, you can meet a lot of different people through there. Prague has a lot of great art museums, go to them. Go to BRNO for a day trip

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to BRNO, go to museums, walk around a lot

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quite easy, is really not that different and a lot (a lot) of erasmus students, so it feels quite international. Obviously (depends on you own language) the language is very different from what im used to, i just used google translate all the time

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: no i didnt do that:( but you should!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: just the language mostly. Its hard eating czech food if you are vegetarian, so thats a bit sad

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the food and people were pretty friendly. Also the cheap beer

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
go around exploring, it really easy to do alone, go to art museum and have a coffee or beer they have great coffee everywhere
do the stuff you actually want to do, dont pressure yourself to go out every night or be friends with people you actually dont like, you should just enjoy things at your own pace
talk to people! people are friendly and want to meet new friends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: i dont think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting so many great friends, trying new different classes and be in a beautiful, lively city that has a lot to offer

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: to be comfortable knowing that i cant do everything, that i need to relax and that its okay to just sleep, but you should probably also get out of your bed

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
